page: OVHcloud d2-4 is a virtual server belonging to the Discovery family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel cores based on the Haswell microarchitecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is limited with a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps, though the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the d2-4 demonstrates entry-level performance, with the majority of tests placing the instance in the bottom 10% tier. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 932.77 and 1818.26 respectively, while the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores reached 632.0 and 1126.0. Memory bandwidth is constrained, measuring 19.19 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 14.22 GB/sec for write operations. For lightweight language model tasks, the server achieves 122.58 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 47.98 tokens/sec for text generation using a small 135M model, though it lacks the capacity to run larger 7B or 70B models.

The shared CPU allocation and low-tier benchmark results represent a clear tradeoff, sacrificing raw processing speed and memory throughput for budget-friendly resource access. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for non-production environments, basic testing, and lightweight utilities. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, which registered a throughput of 1.89 GB/sec, simple Redis key-value operations, basic software compilation, and low-traffic development environments that do not require sustained high-performance compute or guaranteed network bandwidth.
description: OVHcloud d2-4 is an entry-level virtual server in the Discovery family, configured with 2 shared Intel vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor, this instance is designed for low-demand workloads. Benchmark data places its processing, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic performance consistently in the bottom 10% tier, with a single-core Geekbench score of 632.0 and a multi-core score of 1126.0. The server lacks dedicated network bandwidth, making it a poor fit for high-throughput applications. However, it offers a qualitatively cost-effective option for basic development, static web serving, and lightweight testing environments where shared CPU resources and limited memory capacity are acceptable tradeoffs.
